rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e1: The pawn is on c4, and the key squares are b6, c6 and d6. The black king on c7 watches all three.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e2: To bring the king to a key square that the black king is watching, White uses a tool: the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e3: Direct opposition: the kings on the same file, or the same rank, with a single square between them.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e4: The side that does not have the move has the opposition: the other king must move and give way.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d5.2: The black king goes to d7, facing yours with d6 between them: now Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.2: The pawn advanced before the king. The black king goes to c6, right in front of it, and holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e5.1: With this move, Black finds a resource that holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e5.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l1: The kings stand face to face, with c6 between them. Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l2: Zugzwang: being obliged to move when every move worsens the position. If they could pass, Black would stay on c7.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l3: The black king goes to d7 and leaves b6 unguarded.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l4: Your king steps into b6, a key square: the win is guaranteed.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king returns to c8, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l6: Your king goes to c6 and takes the opposition again: Black must step out of the way of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l7: The black king goes to d8, and your king goes to b7, next to c8, the promotion square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l8: With the road clear, the pawn advances to promote.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l9: What if the black king went the other way?
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l10: With the black king on b7, d6 is left unguarded.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l11: Your king steps into d6, another key square, and the win is still guaranteed.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! On c5, your king takes the opposition: face to face with the black king, with c6 between them.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to c5, facing the black king: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn: it is a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always shut the key squares.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's think from Black's side. The opposition is also a defensive tool.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.e2: The pawn is on e3, and the key squares are d5, e5 and f5. The white king on e4 already touches all three.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.2: The white king steps into f5, a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7e8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7e8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f7.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f7.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.2: The white king steps into d5, a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l1: The kings stand face to face, with e5 between them. White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to d4.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l3: The black king follows to d6: Black keeps the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l4: The pawn advances to e4, and the key squares move up to d6, e6 and f6.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l5: The black king goes to e6, right in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l6: The pawn advances to e5, and the black king drops back to e7, always in front of it.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l7: The white king goes to d5.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l8: The black king takes the opposition again, on d7.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l9: The pawn goes to e6, and the black king returns to e7, in front of it.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l10: The white king comes to e5, right behind the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l11: The black king drops back to e8. That way, if the white king goes to d6 or f6, it answers with the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l12: The white king goes to d6.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l13: The black king takes the opposition on d8.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l14: The pawn goes to e7, and the black king returns to e8, in front of it.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l15: With the white king on e6, the black king is not attacked but has no move: this is stalemate, and the game ends in a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! On e6, your king takes the opposition and shuts d5, e5 and f5.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e6, facing the white king: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.1: The kings stand face to face, with c4 between them. Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.2: The pawn is on c2, and the key squares are b4, c4 and d4.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.3: The black king must move. It goes to b5 and leaves d4 unguarded.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.4: The white king steps into d4, a key square.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.5: The black king returns to c6, and the white king settles on c4, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.6: The white king climbs and takes the opposition on c5.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.7: Forced to move, the black king steps aside, and the white king advances to b6.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.curiosida: This pair of positions is an example by Yuri Averbakh (1922–2022), a Soviet grandmaster and one of the greatest endgame experts. He stressed that the opposition is a means: the end is to enter a key square. Averbakh lived to 100, the first grandmaster to reach that age.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.1: The same position, now with White to move. Let's think from Black's side: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.2: The white king goes to b3.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.3: The black king follows to b5: Black keeps the opposition.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.4: The pawn advances to c4, and the key squares move up to b6, c6 and d6. The black king goes to c5, in front of it.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.5: The white king returns to c3, and the black king drops back to c6, in the middle of the key squares.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.6: When the white king goes to d4, the black king takes the opposition on d6.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.7: The pawn goes to c5 and the white king to d5. The black king stays on c7, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.8: The pawn goes to c6, and the black king drops back to c8, in front of it.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.9: The white king goes to d6, and the black king takes the opposition on d8.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.10: The pawn goes to c7 and the black king to c8. With the white king on c6, Black has no move: stalemate.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.11: Same position, the move switched, a different result: whoever has the opposition decides the game.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.1: With 1.f4?, the pawn advances before the king.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king blocks the pawn, and your king cannot reach e6, f6 or g6.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3f2.1: With 1.Kf2?, the king retreats instead of climbing towards e5, f5 and g5.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3f2.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king takes f5 and shuts the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3g2.1: With 1.Kg2?, the king retreats instead of climbing towards e5, f5 and g5.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3g2.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king takes f5 and shuts the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h2.1: With 1.Kh2?, the king retreats instead of climbing towards e5, f5 and g5.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h2.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king takes f5 and shuts the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h3.1: With 1.Kh3?, the king steps sideways instead of climbing towards e5, f5 and g5.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h3.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king takes f5 and shuts the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3f4.1: With 1.Kf4?, the king climbs on the wrong file: it is the black king that takes the opposition.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3f4.2: After 1...Kf6!, the kings stand face to face on the f-file, and Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h4.1: With 1.Kh4?, the king heads for the edge, far from f5.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.err.g3h4.2: After 1...Kf5!, the black king takes f5 and shuts the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play as White and find the best move.
rot.opposition.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king took the opposition, reached a key square, and the pawn advanced afterwards.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8e7.1: With 1...Ke7?, the king leaves the white king's file.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8e7.2: After 2.Kg6!, the white king steps into g6, a key square.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8e8.1: With 1...Ke8?, the king moves away from the key squares.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8e8.2: After 2.Kg6!, the white king steps into g6, a key square.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8g8.1: With 1...Kg8?, the king does not take the opposition.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8g8.2: After 2.Kg6!, the white king steps into g6, a key square.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8g7.1: With 1...Kg7?, the king stands in front of the pawn, but not facing the white king.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.err.f8g7.2: After 2.Kg5!, the kings stand face to face on the g-file, and White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.opposition.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king took the opposition and kept the white king out of the key squares.
